origin: Cohort a2 (gpt-5.6-sol-xhigh) falsified ten of its twelve hypotheses against the coordinator's control plane and returned nine reproducible defects with frozen expected-failure tests. Cohort a6 (gpt-5.6-luna-high) independently found a result-locator self-reference defect and tracked generated bytecode. The coordinator reproduced the two most severe findings directly. This cohort converts those findings into live mechanism changes with recurrence tests, which is the compounding loop the amendment requires rather than a defect list.

ownership_transfer.rationale: The single-writer invariant is what prevents collision, not the identity of the writer. The controller stands off these files for the duration of this cohort so exactly one process writes them, then resumes ownership on ingestion.

units.hypothesis: The generic event command lets a non-coordinator actor append COMPLETED with a fabricated result_commit_id, and the recovery scanner does not notice because it only checks for a missing commit id rather than an unverifiable one.

acceptance.assertion: Actor authority and transition order are enforced for every event kind, not only in cmd_complete: a non-coordinator actor cannot append COMPLETED, PARENT_INGESTED, LEASED or a disposition, and no event may advance a unit out of order. The scanner additionally reports any terminal commit id that cannot be resolved to a real commit. Reproduced by the coordinator on 2026-08-22 with a fabricated commit id that yielded zero reported false completions.
acceptance.falsified_if: any non-coordinator actor can reach COMPLETED, or a fabricated commit id passes the scanner

units.hypothesis: append_event performs an unlocked read-verify-append, so concurrent appends assign duplicate sequence numbers and break the hash chain.

acceptance.assertion: Under at least 200 concurrent append interleavings from separate processes, sequence numbers remain unique and monotonic and the chain verifies, using advisory file locking with a bounded wait and a documented behaviour on lock timeout. Cohort a2 measured 200 of 200 violations before the fix.
acceptance.artifact: hardened append path plus a multi-process concurrency test
acceptance.falsified_if: any interleaving yields a duplicate sequence number or a broken chain

units.hypothesis: Ingestion rejects a fence token lower than the current one but accepts an arbitrary higher one that the coordinator never issued, so a worker can escalate its own ownership.

acceptance.assertion: A fence token is admissible only if the coordinator issued it in a LEASED event for that unit and that lease is the current one; both lower and unissued-higher tokens are rejected and recorded. Cohort a2 measured 10 of 10 unissued higher fences accepted before the fix.
acceptance.artifact: hardened fence check plus recurrence test
acceptance.falsified_if: any fence token not traceable to a coordinator-issued lease is admitted

units.hypothesis: A result_commit_id is accepted as durable on the strength of being a non-empty string, without ever resolving it against a remote, so an invented locator passes.

acceptance.assertion: A terminal result is admitted only after its declared commit is resolved to a real object and its declared artifacts are read back from that exact commit; ten invented locators are rejected. Cohort a2 measured 10 of 10 nonexistent locators accepted before the fix.
acceptance.falsified_if: any unresolvable commit id is admitted as durable

units.hypothesis: The ingestion driver materialises a subordinate branch at its HEAD rather than at the commit each result declares, so it is not reading back by immutable SHA and a later edit to an artifact makes an earlier honest result fail verification.

acceptance.assertion: Artifacts are read back from the exact commit named in each artifact's content_uri, so a result committed earlier still verifies after the branch advances. Demonstrated by the real rejection of a2-u01 for a fault_lab.py hash mismatch caused solely by a later commit on the same branch.
acceptance.falsified_if: an honest earlier result fails because the branch moved on

units.hypothesis: The result emitter stamps the commit that exists at emission time, but the result record itself is committed afterwards, so every result declares a commit that does not contain it.

acceptance.assertion: A result's declared locator resolves to a commit that contains both the artifacts and the result record, or the self-reference is removed and replaced with a scheme that a reader can resolve without guessing. Cohort a6 found five such discrepancies independently.
acceptance.artifact: corrected emitter plus a test that resolves a declared locator end to end
acceptance.falsified_if: a declared locator still cannot be resolved to bytes by a third party

units.hypothesis: Rejecting a corrupt or missing artifact raises an exception but records nothing, so the unit is left in whatever state it was in and the rejection is invisible to recovery.

acceptance.assertion: Every ingestion rejection durably records RECOVERY_REQUIRED with the reason, and committed artifacts are periodically re-hashed so a post-commit corruption is detected rather than assumed away. Cohort a2 measured 20 of 20 rejections leaving no recovery state.
acceptance.artifact: rejection recording plus re-hash sweep plus recurrence test
acceptance.falsified_if: a rejection leaves no durable trace

units.hypothesis: The recovery scanner detects but never remediates, so the commission's requirement of automatic resume or rerun of uncommitted tasks from immutable input is unmet.

acceptance.assertion: An actuator re-leases expired units with a fresh fence, reruns uncommitted units from their immutable dispatch input, resumes checkpointed units at their last checkpoint rather than at zero, and is idempotent under repeated invocation. Cohort a2 measured 0 of 7 in-flight units resuming before the fix.
acceptance.artifact: recovery actuator plus tests covering re-lease, rerun and resume
acceptance.falsified_if: any uncommitted unit requires manual intervention to resume

units.hypothesis: A fresh clone cannot discover subordinate result branches, so total runtime loss loses committed results in practice even though the bytes exist on the remote.

acceptance.assertion: From a fresh clone with no local state, a discovery pass enumerates subordinate result branches from committed configuration plus remote refs and recovers every committed result with verified bytes and hashes. Cohort a2 measured 0 of 10 committed results recovered from fresh clones before the fix.
acceptance.artifact: discovery and recovery pass plus a fresh-clone test
acceptance.falsified_if: any committed result is unrecoverable from a fresh clone
